title: Build a browser photo editor and let the agent test it
summary: A poster had Claude Code build a Photoshop-style editor and test each build in the ego lite browser; he says it caught and fixed an eraser bug wiping the whole image.
agent_role: Claude Code wrote the editor, then used a browser built for agents to click tools, drag sliders, type, undo, and export. It found and fixed its own bug.
outcome: Author reports the agent spotted the eraser wiping the whole picture and fixed it in the next build.
what_they_did: The poster asked Claude Code to build a Photoshop-like image editor in the browser. Using a skill for the ego lite browser, the agent tested each build like a user. It clicked every tool, dragged sliders, typed text, used undo and redo, and exported a picture file.
how_it_went: He says the agent noticed the eraser was wiping the whole image and fixed it in the next build.
worth_knowing: The post is partly a promotion for the ego lite browser, which now also runs on Windows.
prompt: Build a simple image editor that runs in the browser with [tools you want, e.g. brush, eraser, text, sliders, undo, export]. After each build, open it in a browser you control and test it like a real user: click every tool, drag sliders, type text, undo and redo, and export a picture. List any bugs you find, fix them, and repeat. Show me a summary of each round.

curation.rationale: A real build-and-test loop where the agent clicked through its own app and fixed a bug, but the post is hype-heavy and largely promotes a browser product.
